title: Finance & Legal: Integrated Budgeting, Procurement, Contracts, and Revenue Recognition Operational Guidance - 2027
author: Maya Chen
summary: Operational guidance that unifies budgeting & forecasting, contract authority and lifecycle, procurement thresholds and process, and revenue recognition & billing practices. Intended for Finance, Legal, Procurement, and departmental approvers to ensure consistent, auditable decisions and timely recognition/billing across Redwood Inference.
body:
Purpose:
This guidance documents the end-to-end operational procedures and decision rules for: (1) annual budgeting and rolling forecasting, (2) contracts and signature authority, (3) procurement and vendor onboarding, and (4) revenue recognition and billing practices. It is designed to reduce cycle time, limit contract risk, and ensure revenue is recognized consistently with our accounting policy.

Scope:
Applies to all Redwood Inference business units and legal entities for financial planning, vendor contracting, procurement, and customer billing. Exceptions require documented approval from Finance (Head of FP&A) and Legal (General Counsel).

Owners and escalation:
- Primary owner: Finance Ops (finance-ops@redwood.ai)
- Legal owner: Legal Contracts (legal-contracts@redwood.ai)
- Procurement owner: Procurement & Vendor Ops (procurement@redwood.ai)
- Billing owner: Revenue Operations (revops@redwood.ai)
- Escalation path: Department Head -> Head of FP&A -> General Counsel -> CFO

1) Budgeting & Forecasting (annual + rolling 12 months)
- Calendar and cadence:
  1. Jul- Sep: Departmental goal-setting and proposed budget submissions to FP&A.
  2. Oct: Cross-functional alignment; consolidate total company budget.
  3. Nov: Leadership review and scenario planning (base / upside / downside).
  4. Dec 15: Final board-submitted budget.
  5. Monthly: Rolling 12-month forecast updated by the 5th business day.
- Templates and deliverables:
  - Use the official FP&A templates stored in /shared/finance/templates/annual-budget.xlsx.
  - Required deliverables per department: headcount plan, run-rate opex, capital requests (>$50k), and revenue assumptions.
- Approval matrix:
  - Dept owner -> Finance business partner review -> Director-level approval for changes >= $25k -> VP approval for changes >= $100k -> CFO approval for changes >= $500k.
- Variance analysis and controls:
  - Monthly variance report due by day 7. Material variance defined as >5% or $250k for company-wide items; investigate and document root cause in the variance tracker.

2) Contracts & Legal Process
- Contract tiers and signature authority:
  - Standard NDAs and low-risk SOWs (Tier 1): Legal Counsels may approve; signature authority delegated to Director-level PMs up to $50k.
  - Standard customer MSA & SaaS agreements (Tier 2): Legal review required; VP-level signature authority for revenue <= $1M contract term.
  - High-risk or non-standard terms (Tier 3): Any deviation from standard clauses (data residency, indemnity, IP assignments) requires General Counsel sign-off and CFO approval for material financial exposure.
  - Capital and vendor agreements exceeding $250k contract value require Procurement + Legal + Finance review and VP/CFO signature as applicable.
- Contract lifecycle steps (recommended):
  1. Intake: Submit contract request via the Contract Intake form (internal link). Include counterparty, scope, financial terms, and requested signer.
  2. Triage: Legal performs risk tiering and assigns standard template where possible.
  3. Negotiation: Track changes using redline in the contract management system (CMS).
  4. Approval: Required approvers per tier and approval matrix indicated above.
  5. Execution: Signed contract uploaded to CMS and finance notified for booking.
  6. Post-signature: Contract owner to update obligations register and renewal calendar.
- Required contract checklist (minimum):
  - Counterparty legal name and entity
  - Contract start/end dates and renewal terms
  - Pricing and payment terms
  - Termination and liability clauses
  - Data handling and security annex (if applicable)
  - Insurance and indemnity levels
  - Signatory authority confirmation

3) Procurement & Vendor Onboarding
- Procurement thresholds and approval levels:
  - Purchases <= $5,000: Department manager approval; procurement notification recommended.
  - $5,001- $50,000: Department head + Procurement approval.
  - $50,001- $250,000: Director + Procurement + Finance approval; standard contract review by Legal.
  - > $250,000: VP + Procurement + Legal + Finance; Board notification for strategic/long-term commitments.
- Competitive bidding and vendor selection:
  - Competitive bid required for purchases > $50k: min 3 qualified vendors or documented single-source justification.
  - Total Cost of Ownership assessment required for hardware and multi-year software commitments.
- Vendor onboarding checklist:
  1. Verify vendor legal entity and tax information (W-9 / W-8 as applicable).
  2. Confirm insurance certificates and compliance attestations.
  3. Security review (for vendors with data access): complete Security Intake questionnaire and SOC2/ISO evidence review.
  4. Set up vendor in ERP with assigned vendor code and PO terms.
  5. Establish payment terms: default Net 30 unless Procurement negotiates otherwise.
- Purchase Order (PO) process:
  - All purchases > $5,000 require an approved PO before goods/services are ordered.
  - Blanket POs permitted for repeat services with monthly reconciliation.
  - ERPs/PO system (internal guidance): create PO -> obtain approvals per threshold -> send PO to vendor -> match invoice to PO for payment.

4) Revenue Recognition & Billing Policies (summary operational rules)
- Accounting policy reference: Revenue recognized when performance obligations are satisfied in accordance with the company's ASC 606 framework (or equivalent local GAAP). This section summarizes operational rules to support consistent month-end close and billing.
- Recognition rules (operational checklist):
  - Subscription ARR/contracted SaaS: recognize ratably over the contract term from service start date.
  - One-time professional services: recognize when services delivered and acceptance criteria met (document acceptance evidence in CMS).
  - Usage-based billing: recognize when usage is invoiced or reliably estimable; for month-end close, estimate final usage using last 3 months' smoothing if final usage not available and book an accrual/adjustment next month.
  - Upfront payments and prepayments: record as deferred revenue and amortize over the applicable performance period.
- Billing cadence and invoice rules:
  - Standard customer terms: Net 30 from invoice date unless alternate terms negotiated and approved by Finance.
  - Invoice generation: RevOps generates invoices on contract billing schedule (monthly/quarterly/annual). For annual prepay contracts, invoice at contract effective date and book deferred revenue for the service period.
  - Credit memos and refunds: Issued only after RevOps investigation and approval by Finance; document reason and link to contract.
- Dispute and collections process:
  1. Customer dispute received by Support/Sales -> route to RevOps with dispute reason and docs.
  2. RevOps investigates within 5 business days; temporary credit may be issued pending investigation if material.
  3. Collections: unpaid invoices >30 days past due: automated reminder cadence (Day 0, 7, 21, 30) and account owner notified. Escalate to Sales leadership at >60 days and Legal for potential collections actions at >90 days.
- Internal controls and month-end close support:
  - Contract register must be updated within 2 business days of execution to ensure accurate revenue schedules.
  - RevOps to provide a monthly revenue cutoff checklist and deferred revenue roll-forward for FP&A and external auditors.
  - Material manual journal entries (> $50k) require Finance and Controller sign-off and supporting documentation.

5) Operational KPIs & SLAs
- Budgeting/Forecasting: rolling forecast accuracy target: within +/- 3% of actuals for cash and within +/- 5% for ARR by quarter.
- Procurement: PO turnaround time goal: 5 business days for standard purchases; 15 business days for > $50k with competitive bids.
- Contract turnaround: Standard MSA + SOW cycle time target: 7-10 business days for Tier 1/2; Tier 3 subject to Legal negotiation timelines.
- Billing: Invoice generation SLA: invoices created within 3 business days of month close; dispute initial response within 5 business days. Collections DSO target: < 45 days.

6) Reporting and Audit Evidence
- Monthly reports to produce and owners:
  - FP&A: consolidated P&L vs budget and forecast (Finance Ops).
  - RevOps: billing register, aged receivables, deferred revenue roll-forward.
  - Procurement: vendor spend report and open POs (Procurement Ops).
  - Legal: contract register with risk tiering and upcoming renewals.
- Audit evidence retention:
  - Contracts, PO approvals, invoices, and evidence of service delivery must be retained in the CMS/ERP for a minimum of 7 years.
  - Security and compliance artifacts (SOC2 reports, security questionnaires) should be stored in the vendor record and retained per security policy.

Appendices
A) Quick reference approval matrix (summary):
- <= $5k: Dept Manager.
- $5k- $50k: Dept Head + Procurement.
- $50k- $250k: Director + Procurement + Finance (+ Legal if standard contract).
- > $250k: VP + Procurement + Legal + Finance; Board notification for strategic commitments.

B) Sample contract intake fields (minimum):
- Requestor, Dept, Business justification, Counterparty name, Contract type, Value, Contract term, Renewal auto-renew? (Y/N), Special clauses, Requested signer.

C) Common red flags for Legal/Finance to review:
- Indemnity caps not reciprocal or unlimited; unusual IP assignments; trial or refund-heavy clauses; revenue-share models without clear measurement; data residency obligations conflicting with our hosting options.
